item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 042326
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Sun Oct 4 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center has issued its last advisory on
Hurricane Nolo, which has crossed the International Date Line while
located well to the west-northwest of the main Hawaiian
Islands, and continues to issue advisories on Hurricane Rachel,
located a few hundred miles southwest of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico:
A broad area of low pressure is located just to the south of the
Gulf of Tehuantepec. Environmental conditions appear
favorable for gradual development, and a tropical depression is
expected to form during the middle to latter portion of the week
while the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward,
just offshore of the southern to southwestern coast of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sun Oct 04 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 050233
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM MST Sun Oct 04 2026
 
...RACHEL CONTINUES TO MOVE OVER THE OPEN EASTERN PACIFIC OCEAN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM MST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.2N 114.8W
ABOUT 365 MI...590 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...967 MB...28.56 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located 
near latitude 20.2 North, longitude 114.8 West. Rachel is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h). A continued slow 
motion is expected for the next several days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 100 mph (155 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Fluctuations in strength are possible 
overnight, but Rachel is expected to slowly weaken starting 
Monday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 967 mb (28.56 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will continue to affect the coast
of the Baja California Peninsula for the next couple of days.  
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip 
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather 
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Pasch

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 32
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Sun Oct 04 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 050234
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  32
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM MST Sun Oct 04 2026
 
The satellite presentation for Rachel has degraded over the last
several hours as the eye has filled in and the inner core seems to
have come apart as well. Based on water vapor imagery, it appears 
that dry air has managed to make its way into the core of the
hurricane. Using a combination of the most recent TAFB Dvorak fix
and objective intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS, the initial
intensity has been lowered to 85 kt. This level of intensity could
be generous given the structure of the hurricane at this time.
 
Rachel is moving west-northwestward around 6 kt. The high pressure 
system to the north of the cyclone should continue to steer it on a 
generally westward track through the middle of the week. Afterwards, 
the high should weaken and shift eastward as a trough cuts off close 
to southern California. This should cause Rachel to turn back to 
the west-northwest by the end of the week. The current NHC forecast 
track is very close to the previous one, with minor adjustments 
being made based on the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids. 

More fluctuations in intensity are possible overnight for Rachel. 
However, the cyclone is expected to enter a more drier environment 
as it moves farther westward and the sea-surface temperatures are 
expected to be 26C or less in a few days. Therefore, gradual 
weakening is expected to start sometime on Monday and continue 
through the forecast period. The current NHC intensity forecast 
shows a weakening trend similar to the previous one, however the
forecast has been adjusted based on the trends of the HCCA forecast 
aid.
